figures.claim: 1. Figure 1: Comparison of visual token pruning approaches. (Left) D2Pruner requires offline calibration on external data to compute bias priors before deployment. (Right) Our method uses deep-layer (L12) attention directly during inference, eliminating offline calibration while achieving superior performance through semantically richer attention patterns.
figures.explanation: Analysis stage: The repository confirms this architectural claim via: (1) compute_bias_prior.py implements D2Pruner offline calibration; (2) online_prior.py and eval scripts show our method uses raw L12 attention without offline data; (3) d2pruner_baseline/RESULTS.json confirms D2Pruner uses offline bias prior; (4) online_prior/RESULTS.json confirms our method achieves superior 66.32% vs D2Pruner 55.03%. The underlying performance data supporting the bar chart in Figure 1 is present in the JSON result files.

figures.claim: 2. Figure 2: Sensitivity of ratio-based debiasing to shallow layer choice (Ks). Performance varies by 6.47 points across Ks values. Raw attention (dashed line) consistently outperforms all ratio variants.
figures.explanation: Analysis stage: Exact match: layer_choice_stress_test/RESULTS.json reports robustness.range_points = 6.47, and reference_raw_amid.overall_avg = 66.32 which exceeds all Ks variants (K_s=1: 58.49, K_s=2: 61.10, K_s=3: 54.63). The underlying numerical data for the figure is in this JSON.

figures.claim: 3. Figure 3: Spatial analysis of token retention. Our method achieves 43% higher token-bbox IoU (0.212) than FastV (0.148), indicating better concentration of retained tokens around referred objects.
figures.explanation: Analysis stage: Exact match: visualization_analysis/RESULTS.json reports aggregated_spatial_stats: Ours avg_token_bbox_iou = 0.212, FastV avg_token_bbox_iou = 0.148. 0.212/0.148 = 1.432, confirming 43% higher. The underlying data for the figure is in this JSON.

results_section.claim: 1. The improvement is consistent across all 8 benchmark splits, with gains ranging from +9.55 points (RefCOCO+ testB) to +13.64 points (RefCOCO+ val).
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Exact match: online_prior/RESULTS.json and ablation_amid_only/RESULTS.json both confirm per-split values. Ours refcoco+_testB = 57.41 vs D2Pruner refcoco+_testB = 47.86 gives +9.55. Ours refcoco+_val = 64.21 vs D2Pruner refcoco+_val = 50.57 gives +13.64. All 8 splits show positive gains.

results_section.claim: 2. Compared to the no-pruning upper bound (72.06%), our method retains 92.0% of the original performance while reducing visual tokens by 90%.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Exact match: 66.32 / 72.06 = 0.9204 ≈ 92.0%. Both values (66.32 and 72.06) are confirmed in online_prior/RESULTS.json and d2pruner_baseline/RESULTS.json.

results_section.claim: 3. In contrast, D2Pruner retains only 76.4% of no-pruning performance, and FastV retains just 47.0%.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Exact match: d2pruner_baseline/RESULTS.json analysis section confirms 'D2Pruner retains 76.4% of no-pruning performance (55.03/72.06)'. 55.03/72.06 = 0.7637 ≈ 76.4%. FastV: 33.85/72.06 = 0.4697 ≈ 47.0%.

results_section.claim: 4. Figure 2 shows that ratio-based debiasing is sensitive to the choice of shallow layer Ks, with performance varying by 6.47 points across configurations.
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Exact match: layer_choice_stress_test/RESULTS.json reports robustness.range_points = 6.47.

results_section.claim: 5. Our method achieves 43% higher token-bbox IoU (0.212) compared to FastV (0.148) and 20% higher than D2Pruner (0.177).
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Exact match: visualization_analysis/RESULTS.json reports Ours avg_token_bbox_iou = 0.212, FastV = 0.148, D2Pruner = 0.177. 0.212/0.148 = 1.432 (43% higher), 0.212/0.177 = 1.198 (20% higher).
